anchor.exact: Like many languages in the world, Ainu has noun incorporation (hereafter NI) as a productive means for word formation: a noun stem is compounded with a verb stem into one compound verb.

statement.en: Noun incorporation exists in Ainu as a productive word-formation process in which a noun stem is compounded with a verb stem to form a compound verb.
statement.ja: アイヌ語には、名詞語幹が動詞語幹と複合して1つの複合動詞を形成する生産的な語形成手段として名詞抱合が存在する。

entailment.quote: Ainu has noun incorporation (hereafter NI) as a productive means for word formation: a noun stem is compounded with a verb stem into one compound verb.

anchor.exact: In NI of this type, the original subject (koy ‘wave’) is incorporated and the whole verb becomes intransitive. So the original patient (en- ‘me’) can only appear as the ‘subject’ of the NI verb because the NI verb is intransitive and can only take a subject. Therefore, the NI verb (koy-yanke) takes the subjective (not objective) personal prefix (here, ku- ‘I’) which denotes the subject, though semantically it is a patient.

statement.en: In transitive natural force or phenomenon subject incorporation, the incorporation of the original subject detransitivizes the verb, causing the original patient object to promote to subject position marked by subjective personal affixes.

anchor.exact:
NI and QI hierarchy in Ainu

O > S (natural force) > S (possessive) > A (natural force) > O (possessive)

entailment.quote: NI and QI hierarchy in Ainu: O > S (natural force) > S (possessive) > A (natural force) > O (possessive)
